text: 🇲🇽🌎 "Mexico is nobody's backyard. Mexico extends its hand, but never bows its head." — Clara Brugada, Head of Government of Mexico City, Zócalo "Today, when the shadows of imperialist ambition spread again, let us back the President and build national unity." Welcoming Sheinbaum to the Zócalo, the Mexico City mayor called for three unities: of the people, of the Transformation movement, and of the nation. "In a world where winds of hatred blow and war drums sound again, where the far right advances and even fascism resurges, our President's leadership is an international democratic reference."

🇲🇽✊ Mexico City: 70.26 billion pesos in well-being programs for 3 million people in 2026. — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Zócalo, Mexico City 1,377,198 older adults receive their pension, along with 255,000 people with disabilities and 321,684 women aged 60 to 64. Public-school scholarships reach 389,305 high school, 312,885 secondary and 387,867 primary students, and 935,462 children receive low-cost milk. Another ~60 billion pesos go to works: IMSS Hospital 25 in Iztapalapa, a women's cancer hospital, 804 IMSS-Bienestar clinics, Metro Line 12 to Observatorio and Cablebús Line 4. The Zócalo closed a 12-day tour of all 31 states, with some 850,000 attendees.

🇲🇽⚖️ "They stopped being commodities, stopped being privileges, and once again became rights of the people of Mexico." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Zócalo, Mexico City In two years, the Constitution recognized education at all levels, student scholarships, health and housing as rights. The universal pension for older adults and the disability pension became constitutional, the 40-hour work week was approved, and the minimum wage must always rise above inflation. Indigenous and Afro-Mexican peoples are now subjects of public law, and from 2030 no elected office allows re-election.

🔥🇲🇽 "They never understood that this people carries in its DNA the dignity of Hidalgo, the firmness of Morelos, the patriotism of Juárez." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Zócalo, Mexico City "During the neoliberal period, they wanted to make us believe that the country's decisions had to be made in luxury offices, behind the people's backs, handing the nation's assets to a few, dismantling social rights and opening the door to foreign interference. But they were wrong." She traced the people's answer to each betrayal: Ayutla against Santa Anna, Juárez against Maximilian, the Revolution against Porfirio Díaz, and the Fourth Transformation after "36 years of betrayals by neoliberal governments."

🇲🇽🌎 "Sovereignty means that only the people determine the destiny of Mexico." "Since 1814, no foreign power, no economic or political elite has the right to dictate the present and the future of our homeland." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Zócalo, Mexico City She closed her 12-day accountability tour of the country in the Zócalo on September 27, the 205th anniversary of the consummation of Independence. Unlike other Latin American independences led by criollo military men, she said, Mexico's began as a mass popular movement that called for abolishing slavery. "We Mexicans do not want interference, nor interventionism, nor violation of our territoriality."

🇲🇽⚖️ "Article 19 gives the maximum penalty to any foreign agent who tries to violate our territory." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Zócalo, Mexico City In two years of constitutional reforms, the new Article 40 rejects any attempt at foreign interference, Pemex and CFE are again public companies, and water is again a national good and a human right. On Monday the Senate is expected to vote on barring anyone with dual nationality from being governor, head of government or president. "In two years we have reversed a good part of the reforms of neoliberalism that betrayed our history and the struggle of our people."

text:
🇲🇽🏭 <u>WELFARE DEVELOPMENT POLES: $17.5 BILLION COMMITTED</u>

Plan México's Development Poles for Well-being (Podecobi) already have US$17,491.8 million in committed investment, per the Economy Ministry via El Economista. Six of the 14 planned poles have a developer and financing locked in, with Huamantla, Tlaxcala, already operating — backed by 100% immediate income-tax deduction on new fixed assets. Industrial policy is back.

🇲🇽📈 <u>EDOMEX: 1.9 MILLION PEOPLE OUT OF POVERTY</u>

Mexico's most populous state, ruled by the PRI for nearly a century until 2023, now has the numbers: per INEGI's latest measurement, poverty in the State of Mexico fell from 7.4 million people in 2022 to 5.5 million in 2024 — from 42.9% to 31.2%. Delfina Gómez's government has put 55 billion pesos into programs for the elderly, people with disabilities and youth.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MORENA CLOSES RANKS AGAINST FOREIGN-BACKED PRESSURE</u>

Morena leader Ariadna Montiel called for unity ahead of 2027 as the right escalates its campaign against progressive governments across Latin America: "The unity is not around a person, it is around a project… in this moment of harassment of progressive, humanist movements like Morena, we must put the project before the people."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO'S DEBT: THIRD-LOWEST IN THE OECD</u>

Sheinbaum shut down the "debt explosion" narrative: Mexico ranks third among OECD countries with the lowest public debt relative to GDP — far below the US and Japan. And by law, borrowing goes to infrastructure, not current spending. What matters, she said, is "the capacity to pay maturities," and that "is totally guaranteed."
